title: McMath Pierce Solar Telescope Facility with Milky Way

story: A meteor, or shooting star, streaks across the sky above the McMath-Pierce Solar Telescope building, with the Milky Way as the backdrop. The photograph was taken in 2018 and is credited to D. Salman and Kitt Peak National Observatory, part of NSF NOIRLab.

A meteor is the brief streak of light made when a small piece of space debris burns up as it plunges into Earth's atmosphere. The Milky Way is our own galaxy, and the pale band it forms across a dark sky is the combined glow of countless distant stars, seen from inside the galaxy's disc.

The McMath-Pierce facility was built as a solar telescope, but by the time this photograph was released in 2021 it was taking on a new job. The plan was for it to house NOIRLab's outreach centre, the Windows on the Universe Center for Astronomy Outreach, which was expected to open in early 2025.
